newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil to allow private cellular phone services.
newsitem.headline: Brazil to allow private cellular phone services.

text.p: The Brazilian government issued a decree late on Monday authorising the private sector to run cellular telephone services, Gazeta Mercantil said.
Communications Minister Sergio Motta said the decree and the tender documents will be subject to public hearings for 15 days as of Tuesday, the newspaper said.
Motta expects to announce the winners of the concessions to run the so-called Band B cellular services by May 1997, it added.

Brazil will be divided into 10 regions for concessions, which will be valid for 15 years but will be renewable, Gazeta Mercantil said. It also said the government aims to provide cellular services to 10 million people by 2000.
